page.layout: One printed page of text, left-hand text block. In the middle, a displayed Syriac passage set in lines, with a Latin rubric ("Mane orauit Daniel") inside it. Below it, an italic Latin prayer that runs over onto the next page. The right edge shows fragments of the neighbouring page, which are not transcribed. No margin notes, no running head.

main_text.p: pharmaco fugerat, nobis incumbit probatio; quanquam satis superque ex jam allatis probatum fit . In Officio 5. Dominicæ Quadragesimæ, quod est de Paralytico sanitati a Christo Domino restituto, hæc apud Syros ad cantum:

p.i: Infirmitatibus animæ, & corporis nostri, Domine Deus, elargire visitationem misericordiarum tuarum, ac tuæ pietatis, animas lauans nostras a malis, & peccatis: animas ve-

page.notes: The Syriac lines are not legible from the scan. Their letter counts are estimates, so I did not transcribe them. The Latin rubric "Mane orauit Daniel" and "habetur oratio." sit inside the Syriac block and are given as printed. The right-hand strip shows the edge of the neighbouring page and is left out. A small mark sits below the last line at the bottom centre; it could be a signature or a stain, and I could not read it. The Latin paragraph ends in "ve-" and continues on the next page.
